turns.prompt: Produce a compact CAST-style control graph of this incident, focusing on isolation, shared infrastructure, monitoring and response. This is an incident analysis, not a full CAST investigation. Output only newline-delimited JSON objects, no fences or prose. First output exactly six nodes. Node schema: {"type":"node","id":"n1","label":"Short label","boundary":"evaluation|shared|external","role":"controller|process|monitor","detail":"Explanation","pages":[6],"basis":"reported|inferred"}. Choose meaningful components from the report, not chronological events: include the evaluation harness assigning work, agents performing it, the shared Artifactory service, Hugging Face systems, OpenAI monitoring, and incident response. Place harness and agents in evaluation, Artifactory/monitoring/response in shared, and Hugging Face in external. The harness and response are controllers, monitoring is a monitor, agents/services are processes. Assign unique ids n1 to n6. Then output exactly seven edges between those nodes. Edge schema: {"type":"edge","from":"n1","to":"n2","label":"Short label","kind":"action|feedback|failure","detail":"Explanation","pages":[6],"basis":"reported|inferred"}. Include the harness assigning evaluation tasks to agents, Artifactory returning shared agent messages, monitoring alerting response, and response stopping evaluations. Include failed containment of agent access to shared and external infrastructure. Check that each relationship is performed by the FROM component on the TO component: agents move credentials; Hugging Face did not send credentials to Artifactory. Monitoring in this graph is OpenAI monitoring, not assumed visibility into Hugging Face. Use short plain language, not generic root-cause or attack-chain labels. Every label at most three words and every detail at most six words. Pages are the report's printed page numbers. Cite the supporting page for every object. Mark your interpretation of inadequate control or feedback as inferred; mark explicitly described relationships as reported. Focus on the July incident. Do not use May message-board evidence as evidence for a July edge; the July directory-based board is on pages 8 and 9. Use pages 14 to 16 for detection and response. No exploit payloads, commands, credential values or attack recipes. No unsupported links. Total natural-language text at most 140 words.
